title: Getting Around Town
pronunciation_focus_summary: U vs OU — two sounds that English speakers confuse. 'Rue' (street) has the French U (lips forward, tongue front). 'Route' (road) has OU (lips back). Mixing them up changes meaning.

phrases.text: Où est la station de métro ?
phrases.phonetic_ipa: u ɛ la stasjɔ̃ də metʁo
phrases.phonetic_approx: oo EH lah stah-SYOHN duh may-TROH
phrases.pronunciation_notes: 'Où' sounds like 'oo'. 'Station' has the nasal ending. 'Métro' has the French R and closed É.
phrases.example_sentence: Excusez-moi, où est la station de métro la plus proche ?

phrases.pronunciation_notes: The 'ou' in 'tournez' is the back vowel. 'Gauche' — the 'au' sounds like 'oh'.
phrases.example_sentence: Tournez à gauche au prochain feu.

phrases.pronunciation_notes: The 'oi' in 'droite' makes the 'wah' sound. Two French R's close together in 'droite'.
phrases.example_sentence: Tournez à droite après la boulangerie.

phrases.pronunciation_notes: 'Tout' — the 't' at the end is silent. 'Droit' — the 't' is also silent. 'Oi' = 'wah'.
phrases.example_sentence: Continuez tout droit pendant cinq minutes.

phrases.pronunciation_notes: 'Loin' has a nasal vowel at the end. The 'oi' is 'wah' but nasalized here.
The 'è' in 'près' is an open E. French R in 'près'. 'Ici' is simple: ee-SEE.
phrases.example_sentence: Ne vous inquiétez pas, c'est près d'ici.

phrases.pronunciation_notes: This is THE key word for U vs OU. 'Rue' has the French U — lips pursed forward, tongue at the front. NOT like English 'roo'.
phrases.example_sentence: La rue de Rivoli est très connue.

phrases.pronunciation_notes: 'Route' has OU — lips rounded but tongue at back. Compare: 'rue' (y) vs 'route' (u). Different mouth positions.
The 'u' in 'perdu' is the French U. The French R before 'd'. Essential phrase to know!
phrases.example_sentence: Excusez-moi, je suis perdu. Où est la gare ?

phrases.pronunciation_notes: The 'ê' in 'arrêt' is an open E. The French U in 'bus'. Double R in 'arrêt'.
phrases.example_sentence: L'arrêt de bus est au coin de la rue.

phrases.pronunciation_notes: The 'ill' in 'billet' makes a 'y' sound — not 'bill-et'. The 'et' ending is 'eh'.
phrases.example_sentence: Un billet aller-retour pour Lyon, s'il vous plaît.

phrases.text: À quelle heure part le train ?
phrases.translation: What time does the train leave?
phrases.phonetic_ipa: a kɛl œʁ paʁ lə tʁɛ̃
phrases.phonetic_approx: ah kel UHR PAHR luh TRAHN
phrases.pronunciation_notes: 'Heure' has the French 'eu' vowel. 'Train' ends with a nasal vowel. Multiple R sounds.
phrases.example_sentence: À quelle heure part le prochain train pour Paris ?

phrases.pronunciation_notes: Two 'ch' (sh) sounds surrounding a French R. Practice: 'sh-R-sh'. The 'e' is open.

phrases.translation: Can you show me the way?
phrases.pronunciation_notes: The 'in' in 'm'indiquer' and 'chemin' are nasal vowels. 'Chemin' — the 'ch' is 'sh'.
phrases.example_sentence: Excusez-moi, pouvez-vous m'indiquer le chemin pour aller au Louvre ?

phrases.text: C'est à cinq minutes à pied
phrases.phonetic_ipa: sɛt a sɛ̃k minyt a pje
phrases.phonetic_approx: set ah SAHNK mee-NOOT ah PYAY
phrases.pronunciation_notes: The 'inq' in 'cinq' — the nasal vowel plus a 'k' sound. 'Pied' — the 'd' is silent.
phrases.example_sentence: Le restaurant, c'est à cinq minutes à pied.

dialogues.context: Asking for directions on the street

exchanges.speaker: you
exchanges.text: Excusez-moi, je cherche la station de métro Châtelet.
exchanges.translation: Excuse me, I'm looking for the Châtelet metro station.
exchanges.phonetic_approx: ex-koo-ZAY mwah, zhuh SHEHRSH lah stah-SYOHN duh may-TROH shah-TLEH

exchanges.speaker: other
exchanges.text: Bien sûr. Continuez tout droit, puis tournez à gauche à la deuxième rue.
exchanges.translation: Of course. Continue straight ahead, then turn left at the second street.
exchanges.phonetic_approx: byehn SOOR. kohn-tee-NWAY too DRWAH, pwee toor-NAY ah GOHSH ah lah duh-ZYEM ROO

exchanges.speaker: other
exchanges.text: Non, c'est à cinq minutes à pied.
exchanges.translation: No, it's five minutes on foot.
exchanges.phonetic_approx: nohn, set ah SAHNK mee-NOOT ah PYAY

dialogues.notes: Always start with 'Excusez-moi' when approaching a stranger for directions. The French appreciate politeness.

cultural_notes.title: Getting around in French cities
cultural_notes.content: Paris and other major French cities have excellent public transport. The Paris Métro is one of the world's densest networks. Buy a 'carnet' (book of 10 tickets) for savings, or use the Navigo pass for unlimited travel. In smaller cities, buses are the main public transport. When asking for directions, start with 'Excusez-moi' and use 'vous' — the French value politeness highly, and people are generally very willing to help if approached respectfully.
